title: Customer data usage SLA and redaction patterns (workshop draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft capturing customer-facing POC decisions and internal recommended defaults for data usage SLAs, redaction patterns, and minimal-retention deployment options. Target audience: solutions eng, security/compliance, customer engineering, and legal for early-stage pilots where the customer requests tight data controls but still needs live inference telemetry.

Context / constraints observed in recent pilots:
- Customers want fast time-to-insight for model outputs but also strict controls on PII and business-sensitive content.
- Many pilots use ephemeral sessions (chat-style) but send logs/telemetry to Redwood console for debugging; customers are increasingly asking for opt-in telemetry and scrubbed traces.
- Legal teams span a spectrum: from "no retention of conversational content" to "store full transcripts for 90 days for audit". Need patterns to negotiate pragmatic middle-ground.
- Some on-prem/VPC customers cannot allow token-level logs to leave their environment; we need a clear matrix of host vs. client responsibilities.

High-level goals for proposed patterns:
1) Protect direct identifiers (PII) by default while preserving signal for debugging and quality evaluation.
2) Offer clear, short SLAs for retention and deletion that are enforceable via config and automation.
3) Provide a small set of well-documented redaction presets so customers and SEs can align quickly during scoping calls.
4) Keep rollout complexity low: default to a conservative configuration that can be relaxed with explicit customer approval.

Recommended retention tiers (default/negotiable):
- Ephemeral (default for dev/eval pilots): 0 days retention for user messages and model outputs in Redwood logs; only aggregated metrics retained for 90 days.
- Short-term pilot: 7 days retention of full session records, with ability to mark sessions for immediate purge; all audit events retained 365 days.
- Compliance hold (customer-requested): up to 90 days retention for transcripts, with encryption-at-rest using customer KMS and access controls; audit trail required for all retrievals.
- Production baseline (when converted to Dedicated/Private): configurable retention per route, default 30 days for SLA customers, with granular access roles.

Redaction and de-identification presets (apply before logs leave customer environment unless explicitly allowed):
- Preset A: "PII-scrub-basic" (DEFAULT) — Remove names, emails, phone numbers, credit card numbers. Replace with deterministic tokens (e.g., <NAME_#>) to preserve counts without exposing raw PII.
- Preset B: "PII-minimal" — Remove only high-risk fields (SSNs, payment details) and mask emails/phones partially. Keeps more context for QA.
- Preset C: "Context-preserve" — Hash identifiers with salt shared between customer and Redwood for correlation during debugging; requires legal sign-off since hashed IDs are reversible for the holder of salt.
- Preset D: "Business-sensitive redaction" — Customer provides regex/keywords to be redacted; used for vertical-specific secrets (e.g., proprietary IDs).

Telemetry handling (traces, latency, token-level metrics):
- Default: telemetry is aggregated on the Redwood Console (latency percentiles, token counts) without per-session content.
- Opt-in: customers can opt to send full trace dumps for specific sessions; these are stored according to the customer's retention tier and access policy.
- SRE/SE access: require "just-in-time" access with memo + ticket that is logged in audit trail; automated TTL on access credentials for debug window.

Suggested SLA language (short, customer-facing) — use in early proposals:
"Redwood will hold customer POC session data according to the mutually agreed retention tier. For the default Ephemeral Tier, Redwood deletes session payloads within 24 hours and retains only aggregated metrics for 90 days. A customer may request immediate deletion of specific sessions; Redwood will honor requests within 48 hours for POC environments and within 24 hours for Dedicated/Private deployments. All retention and deletion actions are logged and available to customer admins on request."

Minimal technical implementation checklist for pilots:
- Ensure SDK flags to enable redaction preset (A/B/C/D) at client-side before sending data.
- Add server-side enforcement that rejects session data if no preset is selected and customer policy mandates redaction.
- Wire an API hook for "immediate delete" requests with idempotent operation and return of deletion-job id.
- Configure aggregator to store only metrics (no payloads) when Ephemeral tier is selected.
- Integrate KMS for pilot when Compliance hold is chosen; document required KMS parameters for customer.
- Implement an access-review workflow in Console to produce time-limited support access tokens and recorded reason.

Sample DPA addendum clauses (draft language for legal to iterate):
- Data minimization: "During POC, Redwood and Customer agree to limit collection to data strictly necessary to operate the service and debug issues. The default retention for POC session payloads is 24 hours unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- Deletion SLA: "Customer may request deletion of any session or dataset. Redwood will process deletion requests within 48 hours and provide a deletion confirmation id. Deletion is irreversible in Redwood-managed environments; for Private deployments, Redwood will provide an assisted deletion playbook."
- Access for support: "Any Redwood personnel accessing session payloads for debugging will do so under documented justification, time-limited credentials, and all such accesses will be logged and available to Customer auditors on request."

Open questions / scoping flags to bring to customer call:
- Does customer need per-message retention settings (route-level) or is session-level sufficient?
- Will customer provide KMS keys for POC or expect Redwood-managed encryption?
- Are hashed identifiers acceptable for correlation, or must all identifiers be completely removed?
- Regulatory constraints: any sector-specific rules (HIPAA/GLBA/FINRA) that force immutable audit trails or longer retention?

Immediate next steps (internal):
1) Run this draft by Legal (Priya) focusing on the sample DPA clauses and the SLA wording.
2) Build a quick checklist artifact for SEs to send to customers during kickoff.
3) Create a small demo with "PII-scrub-basic" enabled to demonstrate how aggregated metrics still surface useful signals.
4) Track decisions in JIRA ticket JIRA-ENG-9987 and update Confluence page with final presets when approved.

Notes to self (workshop minutes style):
- Diego: confirm tooling to allow client-side redaction toggles in JS/Go SDKs by end of sprint.
- James: prototype immediate-delete endpoint; return deletion-job id so we can reconcile audit logs.
- Priya: draft minimal DPA addendum and circulate to customer legal for pilot.

End of draft — treat as negotiation starting point. Keep conservative defaults; prefer to relax retention only with explicit customer agreement and added controls (KMS, audit reporting, contract clause).
